about.subtitle: Strategy, design, engineering and support for clients across the UK and Europe.
about.body:
DigitalPulse creates fast, maintainable websites for businesses that need more than a template. With 20+ years of web experience, we combine practical strategy, clean UX and dependable engineering across LPCMS, WordPress, WooCommerce and custom PHP/React applications.

We keep the process direct: understand the commercial goal, design the right customer journey, build only what adds value, test carefully and leave you with a website your team can actually own and manage.

faq.title: Questions before you start.
faq.subtitle: Straight answers about scope, pricing, ownership, multilingual websites and post-launch support.

items.question: What types of websites does DigitalPulse build?
items.answer: We build LPCMS landing pages and compact business sites, custom WordPress business and industry websites, WooCommerce stores, and custom PHP/React web applications.

items.question: Do you use templates or create custom designs?
items.answer: Both are possible, but our custom WordPress and WooCommerce pricing is intended for projects with an original layout and design direction. We can also adapt a quality existing theme when budget or timing makes that the better choice.

items.question: How much does a website cost?
items.answer: LPCMS subscriptions start at £3.50 / €4 per month (Premium) or £6.50 / €7 (Premium Pro). Custom WordPress business sites start from £1,690 / €1,890, WooCommerce stores from £3,290 / €3,790 and custom applications from £9,500 / €10,500. Separate prices apply to Latvia. Final prices follow an agreed scope.

items.question: How long does a website project take?
items.answer: A focused LPCMS landing page can move quickly once content is ready. Custom WordPress and WooCommerce projects usually take several weeks depending on content, feedback, integrations and complexity. We agree milestones before work begins.

items.question: Can you help with content and SEO?
items.answer: Yes. We can help organise page structure, improve web copy, set metadata, plan redirects, prepare analytics and build a technically sound SEO foundation. Ongoing content and marketing can be scoped separately.

items.question: Can you host and maintain the website?
items.answer: Yes. Hosting and maintenance can include updates, backups, security checks, uptime monitoring, performance reviews and support for small changes or future development.

items.question: Will I own the website and code?
items.answer: Yes. For custom project work, the agreed website files and custom code are handed over for your use. Third-party plugins, fonts, stock media or services remain subject to their own licences.

items.question: Can the website be multilingual?
items.answer: Yes. LPCMS currently supports 14 language options, and WordPress/WooCommerce multilingual setups can be implemented with an appropriate translation workflow.

items.question: Can you integrate payments, CRM or other systems?
items.answer: Yes. We regularly work with REST APIs, JSON and PHP integrations. Feasibility depends on the third-party system, its API and authentication requirements.

items.question: What happens after launch?
items.answer: We complete a handover, provide practical editing guidance and can continue with hosting, maintenance, support, conversion improvements or new functionality as the site grows.

items.title: LPCMS vs WordPress: choosing the right CMS
items.excerpt: Choose a CMS around editing needs, integrations, scale and maintenance — not popularity alone.
items.body: LPCMS is a strong fit for fast landing pages, compact business sites and projects that benefit from JSON content without a database. WordPress is usually the better choice when a business needs a broader publishing ecosystem, familiar editorial workflows or plugin integrations. The right answer depends on the content model, team, budget and how the website will evolve.

seo.title: LPCMS vs WordPress: choosing the right CMS
seo.description: Choose a CMS around editing needs, integrations, scale and maintenance — not popularity alone.

items.title: What a custom WordPress business website should include
items.excerpt: A strong WordPress build combines discovery, content structure, custom design, reusable editing blocks, QA and a clean handover.
items.body: Custom WordPress should mean more than changing colours on a theme. A solid project starts with goals and information architecture, moves through UX and visual design, then turns the approved system into reusable components your team can edit. Technical SEO, responsive QA, redirects, analytics and launch planning belong in the scope from the start.

seo.title: What a custom WordPress business website should include
seo.description: A strong WordPress build combines discovery, content structure, custom design, reusable editing blocks, QA and a clean handover.

items.title: WooCommerce launch checklist: beyond adding products
items.excerpt: Payments, shipping, tax, transactional email, mobile checkout and analytics all need end-to-end testing before launch.
items.body: A WooCommerce store is only ready when the full buying journey works. Test real product combinations, stock states, coupons, delivery rules, payment outcomes, order emails, refunds and mobile checkout. Then confirm analytics events, search visibility and recovery plans so the store can be supported after go-live.

seo.title: WooCommerce launch checklist: beyond adding products
seo.description: Payments, shipping, tax, transactional email, mobile checkout and analytics all need end-to-end testing before launch.

items.title: Core Web Vitals: performance is part of the customer experience
items.excerpt: Fast pages reduce friction for visitors and give SEO work a stronger technical foundation.
items.body: Performance should be designed into the build rather than added at the end. Keep page structure lean, optimise images, avoid unnecessary scripts, cache intelligently and test on realistic mobile connections. The goal is not a vanity score — it is a page that feels responsive when a real customer is trying to read, compare or buy.

seo.title: Core Web Vitals: performance is part of the customer experience
seo.description: Fast pages reduce friction for visitors and give SEO work a stronger technical foundation.

items.title: When a React web app makes sense
items.excerpt: Use React when the interface is genuinely interactive: dashboards, portals, workflows, live filters or application-like experiences.
items.body: Not every website needs an application framework. React is valuable when users are interacting with stateful data, complex workflows or reusable interface components. For a simple brochure site, a lighter solution may be better. Matching the technology to the job keeps delivery faster and long-term maintenance easier.

seo.title: When a React web app makes sense
seo.description: Use React when the interface is genuinely interactive: dashboards, portals, workflows, live filters or application-like experiences.

items.title: Website maintenance after launch: what to monitor
items.excerpt: Updates, backups, security, uptime, forms and performance need regular attention after launch.
items.body: Launch is the start of the operating phase. A practical maintenance routine checks backups, software updates, security signals, uptime, form delivery, broken links and performance. It should also create space for small improvements based on real user behaviour instead of waiting for the next full redesign.
